extracted.intended_audience: readers of epistolary travel/narrative fiction and social commentary (educated English readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Letters/epistolary travelogue describing places, customs, institutions, and characters; mixes descriptive reportage with social judgment and humorous characterization. Useful as a model or source of evaluative principles for descriptive travel/narrative prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt English idioms and pronunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: “I think the Scots would do well, for their own sakes, to adopt the English idioms and pronunciation; those of them especially, who are resolved to push their fortunes in South-Britain.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that pronunciation strongly influences reception: an English ear is easily influenced and apt to laugh at provincial accents; even eloquent sentiments lose force when spoken in Scotch dialect (example: a member of the house of commons who spoke with energy but failed to engage because of his Scotch dialect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial procedure advantage: examine witnesses apart and jury constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Scottish legislation is founded, in a great measure, on the civil law; consequently, their proceedings vary from those of the English tribunals; but, I think, they have the advantage of us in their method of examining witnesses apart, and in the constitution of their jury..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies concrete procedural practices as evaluative standards for better judicial outcomes — private examination of witnesses and particular jury constitution are presented as improvements over English practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical education: separate theory and practice plus clinical infirmary
rubrics_metrics.description: “The university of Edinburgh is supplied with excellent professors in all the sciences; and the medical school, in particular, is famous... there are different courses for the theory of medicine and the practice of medicine; for anatomy, chemistry, botany, and the materia medica... What renders this part of education still more complete, is the advantage of attending the infirmary...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A model of medical training: distinct courses taught by specialist professors combined with clinical experience at a well-instituted infirmary — presented as a standard of excellence and a reason for the school's fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charitable institutions should employ the poor and be well regulated
rubrics_metrics.description: “Among these, I shall only mention the general work-house, in which all the poor, not otherwise provided for, are employed, according to their different abilities, with such judgment and effect, that they nearly maintain themselves by their labour, and there is not a beggar to be seen within the precincts of this metropolis.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praises well-endowed, admirably regulated hospitals and work-houses that employ the poor according to ability, enabling near self-maintenance and removing visible beggary — Glasgow given as the example that set the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Churches: accept tasteful ornaments and organized psalmody
rubrics_metrics.description: “Even the kirk of Scotland... abounds at present with ministers celebrated for their learning, and respectable for their moderation... Some of their churches have admitted such ornaments... and Psalmody is here practised and taught by a professor from the cathedral of Durham:--I should not be surprised, in a few years, to hear it accompanied with an organ.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues against outdated austerity: acceptance of tasteful church ornaments and trained congregational singing are presented positively, marking moderation and improved taste in worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal government: frequent rotation and trade representation
rubrics_metrics.description: “The magistracy of Edinburgh is changed every year by election, and seems to be very well adapted both for state and authority... the council is composed of deacons, one of whom is returned every year, in rotation, as representative of every company of artificers or handicraftsmen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents annual rotation and representative selection by trade-company as a governance practice that fits both state needs and local authority — an implied civic standard for effective municipal administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Garden and landscape design should follow the genius loci; avoid rigid rows
rubrics_metrics.description: “Though the villas of the Scotch nobility and gentry have generally an air of grandeur and state, I think their gardens and parks are not comparable to those of England... The trees are planted in prudish rows, which have not such an agreeable natural effect, as when they are thrown into irregular groupes, with intervening glades; and firs, which they generally raise around their houses, look dull and funereal in the summer season.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete aesthetic guidance for pleasure-grounds: lay out gardens according to the spirit of the place (genius loci), prefer irregular groupings and glades over straight rows, and be careful about tree species (firs may provide shelter but can appear funereal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ostentatious hospitality; vanity weakens social character
rubrics_metrics.description: “If I may be allowed to mingle censure... their weak side seems to be vanity. I am afraid that even their hospitality is not quite free of ostentation... A burgher of Edinburgh, not content to vie with a citizen of London... must excel him in the expence as well as elegance of his entertainments.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A social judgment that hospitality should be sincere, not competitive display; lavish expenditure to outdo social rivals is presented as a moral/character flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortifications: historical castles may be picturesque but militarily obsolete
rubrics_metrics.description: “The castle... fortifications are kept in good order, and there is always in it a garrison of regular soldiers... but it is incapable of sustaining a siege carried on according to the modern operations of war.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between visual/symbolic grandeur and functional military efficacy — good appearance or tradition is not necessarily equivalent to contemporary defensive utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local characters, anecdote, and vivid sensory detail in travel narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the letters: the storm at sea (nausea, lightning, thunder, drenched passengers), comic characters (Mrs Tabitha, Archy, Mr Humphry Clinker), and richly detailed local customs (pipers, pibrochs, funeral coronach, morning repast of boiled eggs, whisky, bannocks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model for descriptive travel/epistolary writing: enliven reportage with named local personalities, concrete sensory detail, anecdote and humour; balance social commentary with on-the-ground description to engage readers and convey local color.
